question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

We often go camping, but I have never been to that __particular part of town or country__ before.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1**, i.e., "neck of the woods."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"neck of the woods"** refers to a specific area or locality, often where someone lives or is familiar with. (क्षेत्र या इलाका)

 
 
• **Example:** We haven't seen much wildlife in this neck of the woods.
 
 
 
• The idiom used in the sentence emphasizes that the speaker has never visited that particular locality before.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1**, i.e., "neck of the woods."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Knock on wood** (लकड़ी पर दस्तक देना): A superstition to avoid bad luck by tapping on wood.

 
 
• **Example:** I haven’t caught a cold this winter—knock on wood!
 
 
 
• **Get it in the neck** (सजा भुगतना): To be punished or criticized severely.
 
 
• **Example:** He got it in the neck for forgetting his boss’s instructions.
 
 
 
• **Risk one's neck** (अपना जीवन खतरे में डालना): To take significant risks, often involving danger.
 
 
• **Example:** He risked his neck climbing the mountain without proper equipment.
